categories.main_business_segments: Jacobs operates through four main segments: Critical Mission Solutions (CMS), People & Places Solutions (P&PS), Divergent Solutions (DVS), and a majority investment in PA Consulting. CMS focuses on government and commercial clients in areas such as national security, defense, space, and energy. P&PS delivers end-to-end solutions for infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, cities, energy, and water. DVS develops and delivers next-generation cloud, cyber, data, and digital technologies, while PA Consulting provides innovation and transformation consulting services across multiple sectors.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Jacobs leverages advanced engineering, consulting, architecture, design, and project management, with a strong emphasis on digital transformation, data analytics, cloud, cyber, and software solutions. The company uses proprietary software, machine learning, and data science (e.g., through StreetLight Data) to enable technology-enabled solutions, and integrates sustainability and resilience into its project delivery. Its methods include both traditional engineering and cutting-edge digital and scientific approaches.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Jacobs serves a diverse client base, including U.S. federal, state, and local governments, international governments, and private sector clients in industries such as aerospace, defense, automotive, energy, telecommunications, advanced manufacturing, transportation, water, and life sciences. Key customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, Department of Energy, UK Ministry of Defence, and leading private sector firms in infrastructure and manufacturing.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with significant presence in North America (especially the U.S.), Europe (including the UK), Asia Pacific (including India and Australia), and the Middle East and Africa. In fiscal 2023, about 67% of revenue was from the U.S., with the remainder from international markets. Jacobs maintains offices and project sites in over 50 countries.
categories.supply_chain_position: Jacobs primarily operates as a downstream provider in the supply chain, delivering professional services, consulting, engineering, and project management directly to end customers. It acts as a principal contractor or program manager, integrating upstream and midstream technologies and solutions for clients, and often manages subcontractors and suppliers as part of its project delivery.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Jacobs' strategic focus is on high-growth sectors aligned with long-term trends such as infrastructure renewal, sustainability, and digital transformation. Its three growth accelerators are Climate Response, Consulting & Advisory, and Data Solutions. The company invests in R&D for climate adaptation, decarbonization, digital and data-driven solutions, and innovation in consulting and technology-enabled services, with a strong emphasis on ESG and sustainability leadership.
categories.revenue_model: Jacobs generates revenue primarily through cost-reimbursable and fixed-price contracts for professional services, consulting, engineering, and project delivery. In fiscal 2023, 74% of revenue was from cost-reimbursable contracts and 26% from fixed-price contracts. The company also earns revenue from software licensing, proprietary analytics, and long-term program management partnerships.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Jacobs competes with global firms such as AECOM, Booz Allen, KBR, Leidos, Parsons, SAIC, Tetra Tech, WSP, Accenture, Stantec, and others in engineering, consulting, federal IT, and technology services. It is consistently ranked #1 in ENR's Top 500 Design Firms and holds leading positions in program management and combined design/CM-PM services, positioning itself as a technology-forward, sustainability-focused industry leader.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2023, Jacobs reported $16.35 billion in revenue, with net earnings attributable to Jacobs of $666 million. The company has demonstrated steady growth, with revenues increasing 9.6% year-over-year and a backlog of $29.1 billion. Jacobs maintains a strong balance sheet, significant liquidity, and a global workforce of approximately 60,000 employees.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Jacobs differentiates itself through its integrated, technology-forward approach, combining deep sector expertise with advanced digital, data, and sustainability solutions. The company emphasizes its ability to deliver end-to-end, innovative, and resilient solutions for complex global challenges, with a strong commitment to ESG, inclusion, and social value. Its leadership in climate response, digital transformation, and consulting/advisory services underpins its unique value to clients.
